newsitem.title: MEXICO: Tropical Storm Andres moves toward Mexican coast.
newsitem.headline: Tropical Storm Andres moves toward Mexican coast.

text.p: The first of the season's storm systems, Tropical Storm Andres, is closing in on Mexico's southern Pacific coast and could reach land by later Tuesday or Wednesday morning, local weather sources.
"Tropical Storm Andres is expected to continue its movement toward the northeast to the coasts of Chiapas and Oaxaca," the National Weather Service said.

As of late afternoon the storm was located 87 miles (135 km) south of Huatulco, Oaxaca, with winds clocked at 40 miles (65 km) per hour and gusts up to 53 miles (85 km) per hour, it said. Waves were recorded at about 12 feet (four meters).
The service estimated an early Wednesday 0100 local (0600 GMT) landing of the storm. Mexico's marine meteorological service estimated a 1900 local (0000 GMT) landing of the storm.

Resort towns Huatulco, Puerto Escondido, Acapulco and Puerto Angel shut their ports to smaller fishing and tourist craft amid rains. Mexico's crude port that ships to the Far East, Salina Cruz, was also closed to smaller ships.
The Communication and Transportation Ministry warned ships of high waves and winds along the costs of Guerrero, Oaxaca and Chiapas states because of Andres' pending approach.
